accepted.s: Which agency compiles the Gross State Domestic Product (GSDP) of Andhra Pradesh?
o: Directorate of Economics and Statistics, Andhra Pradesh
accepted.x: The Directorate of Economics and Statistics (DES), Andhra Pradesh, compiles the State's GSDP.
accepted.tq: Identify the agency directly responsible for the function.
accepted.sec: State income estimation - AP methods and sectors  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The base year used for the APSES 2024-25 figures is
accepted.x: The APSES 2024-25 figures are presented at 2011-12 base prices.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the officially stated base year from nearby alternative years.
accepted.sec: State income estimation - AP methods and sectors  [APPSC]

accepted.s: In State income accounting, ‘income originating’ refers to
o: Income received by the State Government through taxes
Value produced within the geographical boundaries of the State
Income remitted to the State from abroad
Income earned by residents of the State irrespective of where it is generated
accepted.x: Income originating means the value of goods and services produced within the State's boundaries and corresponds to GSDP.
accepted.tq: Separate the place of production from the residence of income earners.
accepted.sec: State income estimation - AP methods and sectors  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes income accruing to a State?
o: State income plus income of the State's residents earned in other States or abroad
Income earned exclusively by government employees of the State
GSDP minus depreciation and product taxes
Income produced only within the State's geographical boundaries
accepted.x: Income accruing includes State income together with the income earned by the State's residents in other States or abroad.
accepted.tq: Test the distinction between originating and accruing income.
accepted.sec: State income estimation - AP methods and sectors  [APPSC]

accepted.s: For the computation of GSDP in Andhra Pradesh, the economy is divided into how many sectors?
accepted.x: The economy is divided into nine sectors for computing GSDP under the stated classification.
accepted.tq: Use the exact numerical classification rather than a nearby count.
accepted.sec: State income estimation - AP methods and sectors  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following sectors:
1. Agriculture, forestry and fishing
2. Mining
3. Manufacturing
4. Electricity, gas and water
5. Construction
6. Trade and hotels
7. Transport, storage and communication
8. Finance and real estate
9. Community and social services
Which of the above constitute the nine-sector classification used for GSDP computation?
accepted.x: All nine listed sectors form the old CSO classification used for GSDP computation in Andhra Pradesh.
accepted.tq: Check whether the complete sectoral list is retained without omission.
accepted.sec: State income estimation - AP methods and sectors  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?

List-I (Item) | List-II (Treatment)
a. Stamp duties | i. Production subsidy
b. Property taxes | ii. Production tax
c. Apprentice subsidies | iii. Product tax
d. Interest subsidies | iv. Production tax
accepted.x: Stamp duties and property taxes are treated as production taxes, while apprentice and interest subsidies are production subsidies.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure tax-subsidy pairs and eliminate inconsistent codes.
accepted.sec: State income estimation - AP methods and sectors  [APPSC]

accepted.s: State Domestic Product is generally estimated at the State level by using which approach?
accepted.x: States estimate GSDP primarily through the production, or income-originating, approach.
accepted.tq: Match the level of estimation with its principal accounting approach.
accepted.sec: State income estimation - AP methods and sectors  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which development has become available for allocating nationally compiled manufacturing GVA to States?
accepted.x: GST data is now available in addition to the earlier practice of allocating manufacturing GVA according to States' shares in the Annual Survey of Industries.
accepted.tq: Use the institutional-data clue to identify the newer allocation source.
accepted.sec: State income estimation - AP methods and sectors  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The uniform guideline issued by MoSPI in May 2026 for compiling GSVA, with a base year of 2022-23, emphasises
o: Measuring only the organised manufacturing sector
Replacing national accounts with population estimates
Excluding administrative records from State accounts
Integrating administrative records, sector databases and surveys
accepted.x: The guideline seeks to integrate administrative records, sector databases and surveys, while improving coverage of services and the unincorporated segment and consistency with national accounts.
accepted.tq: Identify the precise institutional reform rather than an extreme exclusion.
accepted.sec: State income estimation - AP methods and sectors  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Who associated the national dividend with the net aggregate of commodities and services produced annually by labour and capital acting on natural resources?
accepted.x: Marshall defined the national dividend in terms of the net aggregate of commodities and services produced by labour and capital acting on natural resources.
accepted.tq: Link the economist to the distinctive keyword in the definition.
accepted.sec: Economists' definitions of national income  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Pigou defined national income as the part of the community's income which
o: Includes income from abroad and can be measured in money
Consists only of services received by ultimate consumers
Excludes all income earned from abroad
Represents only additions to capital stock
accepted.x: Pigou's definition includes income from abroad and restricts national income to the portion measurable in money.
accepted.tq: Test the definition through its two identifying elements.
accepted.sec: Economists' definitions of national income  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which economist gave a consumption-based definition of national income, including only services received by ultimate consumers?
accepted.x: Irving Fisher's definition is based on the services received by ultimate consumers.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between economists by the core basis of their definitions.
accepted.sec: Economists' definitions of national income  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The definition of national income as the net output of commodities and services flowing to ultimate consumers from the productive system was given by
accepted.x: Simon Kuznets described national income in terms of the net output flowing to ultimate consumers from the productive system.
accepted.tq: Use the phrase ‘net output flowing to ultimate consumers’ as the identifying clue.
accepted.sec: Economists' definitions of national income  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Marshall included material and immaterial commodities, including services, in his definition.
2. Kuznets linked national income with net output flowing to ultimate consumers or additions to capital stock.
3. Fisher's definition is based primarily on the services received by ultimate consumers.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements correctly describe the respective definitions of Marshall, Kuznets and Fisher.
accepted.tq: Verify each economist-definition pairing before selecting the coded combination.
accepted.sec: Economists' definitions of national income  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The official definition of State Domestic Product emphasises that the value of goods and services is
o: Limited to goods sold outside the State
Counted repeatedly at every stage of production
Produced within the State, counted without duplication, usually during a year
accepted.x: State Domestic Product is the value of goods and services produced within the State, counted without duplication, usually over one year.
accepted.tq: Focus on the qualifying terms ‘within the State’ and ‘without duplication’.
accepted.sec: Economists' definitions of national income  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes the real flow in a two-sector circular flow model?
o: Money moves from firms to households and factor services move from firms to households
Taxes move from government to firms and exports move from households to firms
Factor services move from firms to households and goods move from households to firms
Factor services move from households to firms and goods and services move from firms to households
accepted.x: In the real flow, households provide factor services to firms, while firms provide goods and services to households.
accepted.tq: Separate physical flows from monetary flows in the circular-flow model.
accepted.sec: Circular flow of income - leakages and injections  [APPSC]

accepted.s: In the circular flow of income, factor payments move from
accepted.x: Factor payments constitute the money flow from firms to households in return for factor services.
accepted.tq: Trace the direction of payment against the direction of factor services.
accepted.sec: Circular flow of income - leakages and injections  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is correctly classified as a leakage and an injection respectively?
accepted.x: Saving is a leakage from the circular flow, whereas investment is an injection into it.
accepted.tq: Use the withdrawal-versus-addition distinction to classify paired items.
accepted.sec: Circular flow of income - leakages and injections  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Taxes — Leakage
2. Government spending — Injection
3. Imports — Leakage
4. Exports — Injection
Which of the pairs given above are correct?
accepted.x: Taxes and imports withdraw income from the domestic circular flow, while government spending and exports inject income into it.
accepted.tq: Classify every item before selecting the complete coded option.
accepted.sec: Circular flow of income - leakages and injections  [APPSC]

accepted.s: An economy is in circular-flow equilibrium when
o: Saving alone equals investment irrespective of other flows
accepted.x: Income is in equilibrium when total leakages are equal to total injections.
accepted.tq: Identify the equilibrium condition by equality rather than direction of imbalance.
accepted.sec: Circular flow of income - leakages and injections  [APPSC]

accepted.s: In an open economy, the equilibrium condition for leakages and injections is represented by
o: S + T + M = I + G + X
C + S + X = I + T + M
S + I + T = M + G + X
S + T + X = I + G + M
accepted.x: The three leakages are saving, taxes and imports, while the three injections are investment, government spending and exports.
accepted.tq: Place withdrawals on one side and additions on the other side of the identity.
accepted.sec: Circular flow of income - leakages and injections  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT a major difficulty in measuring national income in India?
o: A well-documented and fully accounted informal sector
Black money and parallel economic activity
accepted.x: The informal sector is difficult to measure because it often lacks proper accounts; a well-documented and fully accounted sector would not constitute the stated difficulty.
accepted.tq: Find the option that reverses a recognised measurement problem.
accepted.sec: Difficulties in measuring national income in India  [other exams]

accepted.s: A farmer consumes part of the crops produced on his own farm without selling them in the market. This creates difficulty in national-income estimation mainly because of
accepted.x: Farm output retained for home use is non-monetised and may not enter market records, making its valuation difficult.
accepted.tq: Apply the measurement problem to a concrete subsistence-production situation.
accepted.sec: Difficulties in measuring national income in India  [other exams]

accepted.s: The absence of proper accounts in a large informal sector, together with illiteracy and missing records, primarily affects the estimation of
o: Only the price of imported goods
accepted.x: Lack of accounts, illiteracy and missing records make it difficult to capture the actual level of economic activity in the informal sector.
accepted.tq: Connect poor documentation with incomplete coverage of output and income.
accepted.sec: Difficulties in measuring national income in India  [other exams]

accepted.s: A person simultaneously works as a farmer and a weaver. This illustrates which difficulty in national-income measurement?
accepted.x: When individuals perform several occupations, classification of their output and income becomes difficult because occupational specialisation is absent.
accepted.tq: Infer the accounting difficulty from the worker's multiple occupations.
accepted.sec: Difficulties in measuring national income in India  [other exams]

accepted.s:
Which combination represents difficulties associated with valuation in national-income accounting in India?
1. Risk of double counting
2. Valuation of depreciation
3. Valuation of inventories
4. Existence of black money or a parallel economy
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Double counting, valuation of depreciation and inventories, and unrecorded black-money activity all complicate national-income estimation.
accepted.tq: Group related accounting and recording problems before choosing the code.
accepted.sec: Difficulties in measuring national income in India  [other exams]

accepted.s: Rapid population growth makes which comparison more difficult?
o: Comparison of total exports between two months
Per capita income comparisons over time or between regions
accepted.x: Population growth changes the denominator in per capita measures and therefore complicates comparisons of per capita income.
accepted.tq: Identify the denominator effect in per capita indicators.
accepted.sec: Difficulties in measuring national income in India  [other exams]

accepted.s: The IMF has flagged persistent gaps between production-side and expenditure-side GDP in India as indicating, among other things,
o: A permanent fall in government expenditure
Complete capture of all informal activity
accepted.x: The IMF review identified gaps between the two approaches as evidence of partial capture of informal activity, among other data limitations.
accepted.tq: Interpret the implication of a discrepancy between two accounting approaches.
accepted.sec: Difficulties in measuring national income in India  [other exams]

accepted.s:
Which of the following was identified as a data limitation in the IMF review of India's national accounts?
1. Lack of seasonally adjusted quarterly data
2. Delays in gross fixed capital formation by institutional sector
3. Persistent production-expenditure discrepancies
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: The review referred to all three issues: the absence of seasonally adjusted quarterly data, delays in GFCF data by institutional sector and persistent discrepancies between production and expenditure estimates.
accepted.tq: Check each listed data limitation before accepting the comprehensive option.
accepted.sec: Difficulties in measuring national income in India  [other exams]

accepted.s: The use of Supply and Use Tables in the new national accounts series is intended primarily to
o: Exclude the unorganised sector from national accounts
Reduce the discrepancy between production and expenditure estimates
Replace GSDP with per capita income
Increase the discrepancy between production and expenditure estimates
accepted.x: Supply and Use Tables are used to reconcile supply and expenditure data and thereby reduce the discrepancy between the two sides of GDP estimation.
accepted.tq: Identify the purpose of the accounting reconciliation tool.
accepted.sec: Difficulties in measuring national income in India  [other exams]

accepted.s: After the benchmark year, household-sector GVA is extrapolated using
accepted.x: Household-sector GVA is extrapolated after the benchmark year using suitable indicators.
accepted.tq: Recall the specific post-benchmark estimation procedure.
accepted.sec: Difficulties in measuring national income in India  [other exams]

accepted.s: The private corporate segment in national-accounts estimation depends substantially on which database?
accepted.x: The private corporate segment relies substantially on data from the Ministry of Corporate Affairs (MCA) database.
accepted.tq: Match the institutional segment with its principal database.
accepted.sec: Difficulties in measuring national income in India  [other exams]
